title: An array that grows
hints: Only grow when the array is full (`len == cap`). The new capacity is `cap == 0 ? 4 : cap * 2`, and `realloc(NULL, n)` behaves like `malloc(n)`, so the first push needs no special case.

`realloc` takes a size in **bytes**: `new_cap * sizeof *v->data`. Store its result in a temporary first. If it's `NULL`, the old block is still valid and still yours, so return `false` without touching `v`.
`int *grown = realloc(v->data, new_cap * sizeof *grown); if (grown == NULL) return false; v->data = grown; v->cap = new_cap;` then `v->data[v->len++] = value;`. Free: `free(v->data); intvec_init(v);`
